AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is domestic hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping the home and its surroundings clean
   B. Washing your own body
   C. Growing food
   D. Cooking meals

2. Why should a rubbish bin have a lid? (1 mark)
   A. To look pretty
   B. To make it heavy
   C. To keep out flies and rats
   D. To stop rubbish from rotting

3. Which waste should not be burnt because the smoke is harmful? (1 mark)
   A. Dry leaves
   B. Paper
   C. Plastic
   D. Wood

4. What is the correct order for cleaning a room? (1 mark)
   A. Mop, dust, sweep
   B. Sweep, mop, dust
   C. Dust, sweep, mop
   D. Mop, sweep, dust

5. Which PPE keeps dust from being breathed in? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Headgear
   C. Gumboots
   D. Overall

6. Why should rubber boots not be dried in very strong heat? (1 mark)
   A. The rubber can crack
   B. They get heavier
   C. They grow
   D. They become cleaner

7. How should an overall be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it wet
   B. Wash with soap, rinse and dry in the sun
   C. Wipe it with a dry cloth only
   D. Burn it

8. What should you do after cleaning PPE? (1 mark)
   A. Wash your hands with soap
   B. Eat without washing
   C. Wipe them on clothes
   D. Play in mud

9. How should gumboots be dried? (1 mark)
   A. In a closed cupboard while wet
   B. Beside a hot fire
   C. Under a heavy weight
   D. Upside down in a shady, airy place

10. Which PPE protects the head from sun and dust? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Headgear
   C. Gumboots
   D. Gloves

11. Why is a display of clean PPE useful? (1 mark)
   A. It helps others learn about PPE and hygiene
   B. It wastes time
   C. It makes PPE dirty
   D. It hides the PPE

12. Which is a type of tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. Cross stitch
   B. Even tacking
   C. Chain stitch
   D. Satin stitch

13. Which tool holds a needle safely on the finger to push it? (1 mark)
   A. Thimble
   B. Pin cushion
   C. Ruler
   D. Scissors

14. Which thread colour is best for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Black on black
   B. White on white
   C. One matching the cloth exactly
   D. One that shows clearly on the cloth

15. How should you finish a line of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. With scissors
   B. With a very big knot
   C. With a small back stitch
   D. By pulling the thread out

16. What is the use of a scarecrow shirt made with tacking? (1 mark)
   A. It is a tool
   B. It is eaten
   C. It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   D. It waters plants

17. In long and short tacking, the pattern is (1 mark)
   A. A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   B. No stitch
   C. All gaps long
   D. All stitches short

18. How much of each edge is folded twice for the handkerchief hem? (1 mark)
   A. 1 mm
   B. About 1 cm each time
   C. 10 cm
   D. 20 cm

19. How long should a length of thread be for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. As long as the room
   B. About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm
   C. 1 cm
   D. 10 metres

20. What do you use to mark a straight line on cloth? (1 mark)
   A. A broom
   B. A plate
   C. A hammer
   D. Chalk and a ruler

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how stagnant water around the home can lead to disease and how to prevent it. (4 marks)

22. Name three PPE items and say what each protects. (3 marks)

23. Describe how to make a handkerchief hem using tacking. (4 marks)

24. Plan a group project of making a scarecrow shirt using tacking. Give materials, steps, safety and how the group shares work. (5 marks)

25. State three safety rules when using needles and scissors. (3 marks)

26. How should cloth items such as overalls and cloth masks be cleaned? (3 marks)

27. Name two types of tacking stitches and describe each. (3 marks)

28. List the tools and materials needed for tacking. (3 marks)

29. Why should plastic not be burnt? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Keeping the home and its surroundings clean
   It is care of the home environment.

2. C — To keep out flies and rats
   Lids stop pests.

3. C — Plastic
   Burning plastics gives harmful smoke.

4. C — Dust, sweep, mop
   Dust falls, so dust before sweeping.

5. A — Dust mask
   A mask covers the nose and mouth.

6. A — The rubber can crack
   Heat damages rubber.

7. B — Wash with soap, rinse and dry in the sun
   Sunshine helps to kill germs.

8. A — Wash your hands with soap
   Hands can carry germs.

9. D — Upside down in a shady, airy place
   This drains water and protects the rubber.

10. B — Headgear
   Hats, caps and scarves cover the head.

11. A — It helps others learn about PPE and hygiene
   Displays teach and encourage others.

12. B — Even tacking
   Even tacking is taught in Grade 4.

13. A — Thimble
   A thimble protects the finger.

14. D — One that shows clearly on the cloth
   It is easy to see and pull out.

15. C — With a small back stitch
   Tacking must be easy to remove.

16. C — It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   Tacking holds the shirt pieces together.

17. A — A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   The pattern alternates.

18. B — About 1 cm each time
   The raw edge is hidden.

19. B — About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm
   Long thread tangles.

20. D — Chalk and a ruler
   Chalk marks show the line.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mosquitoes breed in it and spread malaria. Empty tins and tyres, fill puddles, and drain water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for breeding, 1 mark for disease, 2 marks for prevention.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud and water; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cut a 25 cm square; fold each edge twice by about 1 cm; pin; tack along the fold with even tacking; check evenness; sew permanently and remove tacking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: old cloth, needles, thread, scissors, chalk, ruler. Steps: measure and cut two pieces; pin; tack along sides; leave openings; sew firmly; stuff. Safety: count needles. Group: share tools, assign jobs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark materials, 2 marks steps, 1 mark safety, 1 mark teamwork.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never put needles in the mouth; keep them in a pin cushion; count them; carry scissors with points down (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash with soap and water, rinse well and dry in the sun to help kill germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking has equal stitches and gaps; long and short tacking has a long stitch followed by a short stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each name and 1 for correct descriptions.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Needle, thread, scissors, ruler or tape measure, chalk, pins, cloth, thimble (any correct materials).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: The smoke is harmful to health and the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harmful smoke, 1 mark for the environment or health.
